name: complex-geometry
title: Complex geometry: gmsh-generated non-trivial domains
question:
Does a real gmsh-constructed non-trivial planar geometry -- imported into
dolfinx via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh` -- produce a genuine
unstructured triangulation with a positive cell count, and does a real
Poisson solve on that imported mesh (homogeneous Dirichlet boundary, a
constant interior source) stay finite, bounded, and non-trivially
nonzero, across three qualitatively different domain topologies (a
simply-connected domain with a circular hole, a non-convex re-entrant
corner, and a multiply-connected annulus)?
hypothesis:
The gmsh -> dolfinx import path is standard and robust for any of these
three domains, so each should import with a cell count well above a
trivial handful, and -Laplacian(u) = 1 with u=0 on the full boundary
should have a smooth, non-negative (maximum-principle), interior-peaked
solution on every one of them -- confirming the FEniCSx bridge works on
genuinely non-trivial, non-rectangular domains, not only the unit square
every other study in this investigation uses.
objective:
Build the `complex_geometry` composite (a single `ComplexGeometryStep`:
gmsh geometry construction -> dolfinx import -> Poisson solve) for each of
the three named geometries (obstacle, L-shape, annulus) and verify (a)
each mesh imports with a positive, non-trivial cell count and (b) each
solve returns a finite, bounded, non-trivial solution field.
description:
Wraps a single `ComplexGeometryStep` in the `complex_geometry` composite
generator (Task 11). The Step is stateless -- given only a named geometry
+ mesh resolution + polynomial degree, it: (1) builds the geometry with
the real gmsh Python API (`viva_fenics.fem_gmsh`) -- constructive solid
geometry (`gmsh.model.occ`) boolean cuts producing an obstacle domain
(unit square minus a circular hole), an L-shaped domain (unit square minus
its upper-right quadrant), or an annulus (outer disk minus a concentric
inner disk); (2) imports the resulting unstructured triangulation into a
dolfinx `Mesh` via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh(gmsh.model, comm, rank,
gdim=2)`; and (3) solves the Poisson equation -Laplacian(u) = 1 with a
homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition on the FULL exterior boundary
(including the inner hole boundary for obstacle/annulus) -- a real
`dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` assembled and solved on the imported
mesh's true cells, not the unit square every other study in this
investigation uses.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study: it is the investigation's only
demonstration that the FEniCSx bridge works on genuinely non-trivial,
gmsh-generated domain topologies (a hole, a re-entrant corner, a
multiply-connected ring), not just the unit square's built-in structured
triangulation every other study relies on.

expected_behavior.name: mesh-imports-with-positive-cells
expected_behavior.en: Each of the three gmsh geometries (obstacle, lshape, annulus) imports into a dolfinx mesh with more than 20 cells at resolution=32.
expected_behavior.rationale: A real gmsh triangulation of any of these domains at resolution=32 (target element size h=1/32) should produce hundreds of triangles; a near-zero or trivial cell count would indicate a degenerate/empty geometry was silently imported (e.g. a failed boolean cut).

expected_behavior.name: solution-finite-bounded-nontrivial
expected_behavior.en: The Poisson solution on each geometry is finite everywhere, non-negative everywhere (maximum principle), and reaches a max value above 1e-6 (non-trivially nonzero) and below 1.0 (bounded).
expected_behavior.condition: 1e-6 < max(solution) < 1.0 and min(solution) > -1e-8 and all(isfinite(solution)) for every geometry
expected_behavior.rationale: -Laplacian(u) = 1 with u=0 on the boundary has a smooth, bounded, strictly-positive-interior solution by the maximum principle for any of these domains; a NaN/Inf, an all-zero solution, or a negative value would indicate the boundary condition or the imported mesh's orientation/connectivity was broken.

behavior_tests.name: mesh-imports-with-positive-cells
behavior_tests.description:
n_cells (the imported dolfinx mesh's local cell count, read directly
off `domain.topology.index_map(tdim).size_local`, not estimated) for
EVERY one of the three geometries (obstacle, lshape, annulus) at
resolution=32 must exceed 20.

provenance.note: Observed cell counts at resolution=32 run in the low thousands for all three geometries (see studies/complex-geometry/sims/run.py's printed summary); 20 is a generous floor that only fails on a genuinely degenerate/empty import, not on any real triangulation density.

behavior_tests.name: solution-finite-bounded-nontrivial
behavior_tests.description:
For every one of the three geometries, the Poisson solution
(-Laplacian(u)=1, u=0 on the full boundary) must be finite everywhere,
non-negative everywhere, and reach a max value strictly between 1e-6
and 1.0.

provenance.note: The maximum principle for -Laplacian(u)=const>0 with u=0 on the boundary guarantees a smooth, non-negative, interior-peaked solution on any of these domains; a solution that is all-zero, negative anywhere, or non-finite indicates a broken boundary condition or a corrupted imported mesh, not solver noise.

behavior_tests.name: solution-stays-bounded
behavior_tests.description:
The Poisson solution's max value on every geometry must stay below 1.0
-- no blow-up from a malformed imported mesh (e.g. inverted-orientation
cells corrupting the stiffness-matrix assembly).

provenance.note: Observed peak solution values at resolution=32 sit around 0.01-0.04 across all three geometries (see run.py's printed summary); 1.0 leaves two orders of magnitude of headroom while still catching a genuine assembly/orientation blow-up.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
complex-geometry; it is the investigation's non-trivial-domain
showcase, built directly on the validated dolfinx bridge
(poisson-validation) rather than on the scalar diffusion/reaction
studies -- it needs a correct FEM solve, not the transient stores this
investigation's other advanced studies build on.
